audience.audience: The primary household milk-decider — the mother in a quality-conscious urban/peri-urban South Indian family, buying daily via general trade or home delivery, currently splitting between loose milk and a branded pack
audience.believes_now: Loose milk is fresher and cheaper; branded milk is convenient but I'm paying for a name. I worry about adulteration but don't have a reason to trust one pack over another.

channel.channel: Outdoor / transit near residential clusters and schools
channel.job: Own the two milk moments (before school, before bed) in the physical neighbourhood; keep #PureDoodhKiShakti present at the point of routine
channel.measure: coverage of target catchments; cost per reach

occasion.occasion: The first tumbler before school and the last glass before bed — the two milk moments that bookend a child's day
occasion.channels: Regional TV + CTV (lead); Outdoor/transit near residential clusters and schools; YouTube + regional social
occasion.hands_over: Built emotional-pillar awareness and neighbourhood presence around the two milk moments; hands warmed, primed households to the conversion phase

measure.leading: Building 1+ reach against target households in core Telugu/Kannada/Tamil geos; completed-view rate on the emotional film in the same geos
measure.lagging: 1+ reach % of target households achieved at planned cost per reach point; unaided awareness of Heritage against the two milk moments
measure.would_tell_us_it_failed: Reach curve flattens below target before the buying-occasion window opens, or cost per reach point runs materially above plan, i.e. we are paying reach money for frequency against people already reached

message.text: Social — Reel/Short, mother's POV: the two milk moments cut back to back — first tumbler before school, last glass before bed — with the farmer's dawn footage spliced between. Caption: 'The small, everyday choices are what quietly make them strong. #PureDoodhKiShakti #HeritageFoods'
message.note: Owns the bookend occasion in the feed's native language — the emotional message as a mother would actually say it, shareable because it's her routine, not an ad.
